title: Netero's Final Prayer Was a Checkmate

cuts.voiceover_text: Netero faces Meruem in the ruined chamber, moving so quickly that the King can barely follow his afterimage. Then the old man brings his hands together and returns to prayer, summoning the golden form of the hundred-type Guanyin Bodhisattva.

The exchange leaves Netero's left arm severed and bleeding on the floor. He steadies himself on one knee while Meruem watches without flinching, and the old man's expression hardens instead of breaking.

Netero raises his remaining hand and begins the final exchange. The Guanyin strikes from every angle as Meruem absorbs the assault, while thousands of impacts erupt into showers of sparks. Beneath the chaos, Meruem studies the tiny bias in Netero's movements and finally finds a path through the defense.

With the King in front of him, Netero gathers the last of his aura into the Guanyin's enormous palms. The statue closes around Meruem, and the old man's entire body becomes a blinding point of light before Zero Hand fires with a merciless roar.

After surviving the attack, Meruem approaches the wounded Netero and asks one final question: what is his name? Netero answers clearly, giving the King the name Meruem's mother gave him, and the King can barely process the dignity of the answer.

Then Meruem sees the resolve in Netero's face and feels true fear for the first time. The old man is not waiting helplessly for death; he is warning the King with the cold certainty of someone who has already prepared the final move.

Netero reveals the miniature bomb inside his chest, designed to detonate the instant his heart stops. He tells Meruem he will see him in hell, and the King realizes that checkmate belonged to Netero from the beginning. The heart stops, the Poor Man's Rose erupts, and the battlefield disappears beneath the blast.
